commit.message:
feat(import): read SolidCraft face names beside the .sc final body

The Solidcraft reader reads the name of each record face of the final
body from model cache format 10 (`model.names[model_bodies[m].names]`:
`faces` and the `verified` and `former` items of `info`). One name for
each record face, in record order. A cache of another format gives no
names and no note. Names that do not fit the body give no names and one
note; they never refuse the import.

Pins: names read with four- and five-item info; every triangle of a
named face lies on that face's plane (a block of our own, with a shifted
list as the negative control); each misfit gives a note; format 8 reads
none; the SolidCraft-written hole_on_pocket_wall.sc names its caps in
record order; hostile names records never panic or refuse.

Built and tested on the earlier base 773736856 (the PR body lists the
runs). Rebased onto a721fd4dc without a local build; the maintainer's
runners test it.

Refs #3915

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(import): hold the .sc face names beside the model's facets

The Solidcraft import builds facet ranges from the machining mesh's
`tri_face` (one range for each run of a record face) and hands them out
with SolidCraft's names as `geometry::source_faces::SourceFaces`, beside
the mesh. A record that does not tile the facets is dropped with a note.

In the app, `Graded` and `ImportModel` carry it, and a new component
(`schema::SourceFaces`, through `source_faces::{of, set}`) holds it on
the model in memory only. It keeps the revision and facet count it was
landed with, so any other landing of facets makes it stale. UpdateModel
trades it on undo (`with_source_faces`); unstated, an update drops it,
so a repair or a file that is not `.sc` drops the names. DeleteEntity
puts it back on undo. The window, script/MCP import and fixture
re-import pass it. Nothing reads it yet and the project file is
unchanged: no behaviour change.

Built and tested on the earlier base 773736856 (the PR body lists the
runs). Rebased onto a721fd4dc without a local build; the maintainer's
runners test it.

feat(geometry): find a missing face's successor by its SolidCraft names

The new module camcraft_geometry::source_follow takes two revisions of
one model, each with its source face record, and a face or patch id
that went missing. It gives the one new feature with the same
SolidCraft names, or the reason that there is none.

A follow happens only when the names leave no doubt:
- the id was in the old revision only, on exactly one feature;
- no other old feature of that kind has the same names;
- every old name is verified;
- exactly one new feature of the same kind has the same names, where a
  record face's former name counts too (Split Face pieces);
- that feature is new, its names are verified, and a face keeps its
  plane kind.

The module is pure (features and records in, an id or a reason out),
so it lives in the geometry crate. Table tests on a box at two widths
and a faceted cylinder whose wall is one patch, with names of our own
in a different record order per revision.

feat(project): save a .sc model's source face record, with no version step

A model with a source face record saves it under the optional entity
key `source_faces`: the names in record order, and [start, end, face]
facet ranges. The DTO is in the new project/source_faces_dto.rs. The
hooks are one line each in entity.rs, wire.rs and apply.rs.

- PROJECT_VERSION does not change (D4, the `solids` #917 precedent).
  An old reader drops the key and reads the model as today. This is
  the maintainer's call (Q1).
- At save, only a record that tiles the facets is written.
- At load, a record that does not read, does not tile the facets,
  names a face past u32, or holds a name over 16 KiB is dropped with
  a logged note. The key never refuses a project.

feat(import): face picks follow their SolidCraft names at a re-import

When a .sc model imports again, a face or patch pick inside an
operation that the geometry hash no longer finds follows the face
with the same SolidCraft names, in the update's own undo step.

- The new commands/update_model_follow.rs snapshots the old record and
  the operations with a face or patch pick on the model in
  UpdateModel::new, and decides the follow in with_source_faces, the
  step that brings the new record. update_model.rs gets hooks only.
- The walk covers every pick store inside an operation (D7): the
  source selection, the extra and open boundaries, "Do not touch" and
  the two deburr exclude lists. A test checks each store.
- Each operation with a followed pick gets one needs_review line. The
  line holds the post until mark_operation_reviewed (D5). The line is
  cleaned and cut to 240 bytes, so the project always loads (D10).
- Each pick that could not follow stays as it was and is named with
  its reason: in the window's re-import phrase (UpdateModel::summary)
  and in the `picks` key of the cam.import / MCP import_model answer.
  Generation refuses it as before (D6).
- Not followed: setup WCS and alignment picks, fixture-locate picks,
  electrodes, chains and vertices.

The tests join the model_link binary: model_link/follow.rs,
face_record.rs and the source_names.rs fixtures. Decisions D4-D10 are
in this change's file in docs/decisions/.

fix(import): no follow for Probe and Slot picks, and no two picks on one face

Fixes from a review of the name follow:

- A Probe's or a Slot's pick writes numbers into its parameters when
  it is made (probe_from_picks, slot_from_picks), and generation keeps
  those numbers. A followed pick would keep the old face's numbers
  against the moved face. Such picks now never follow: they stay as
  they were and are reported lost with "its pick set the operation's
  numbers - pick it again" (stores::seeds_from_picks, D7).
- source_follow: a new face that answers to the names of two old
  faces (one by name, one by its former name) takes neither pick
  (Lost::Shared, D8). Pinned by two_old_faces_never_meet_on_one_new_face.
- ImportFixture::update_summary reads UpdateModel::summary, so a
  fixture's re-import in the window names the lost picks too (D6).
- D5 says that a follow skips the pick-time gates, with generation as
  the backstop for the pick's shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(import): the name follow builds its own features, not a cached facet order

The follow read both revisions through model::features_of_shared,
which falls through to the features cache of features_of_local. That
cache keys a mesh by an order-free content digest (digest_of). So a
mesh with the same triangles in another facet order, seen earlier on
the thread, can give its facet indexes to the new mesh. The source
face record names facets by index, so the follow could give a face
the name of another face and move a pick to the wrong face.

The follow now builds the two revisions' features from their facets
(feature::features_of_facets). The ids do not change, because they
hash positions, not indexes. The cost is two feature builds at a
re-import that has a pick to follow.

Pinned by model_link::facet_order: the reversed facet order of the
new mesh is put into the cache first, and the front pick must follow
the front face, read from the facets directly. D8 records it.

Not compiled: this commit came after the local runs, and it is pushed
without a local build. The maintainer's runners test it. The pin is
not seen red without the fix yet.
